A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RMR study. The main text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–G are readable and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original dynamical-system simulations, LLM decoding experiments, spectral analyses, and judge evaluations, including additional experiments in Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulations and experimental results, including the multi-prompt and multi-model appendix evaluations and Table 1.

M1.justification: Equation (9) changes the reported update from V_t <- (I - ηΓ)V_t(I - UU^T) to V_t <- V_t - ηΓV_tUU^T. This corrects the damping step to attenuate only the selected subspace. Eigenspace estimation, thresholding, and other RMR components remain unchanged; implementation changes or reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the IFS simulations and SEP long-form continuation evaluations, including HEIDEGGER and the 60-text appendix experiment. Dialogue, RAG, code generation, and reasoning are mentioned only as future coverage in v3.

E2.justification: Figure 5 retains standard decoding, typical sampling, and random regulation as comparators. Appendix F retains the same standard-decoding versus RMR comparisons; no evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Decoding filters, completion lengths, correlation-dimension threshold, model configurations, and judge protocol are retained. Figure 2(b)'s temperature of 1.0 is newly disclosed for the existing trajectory, without evidence of a changed experiment.

E4.justification: The random-regulation control, spectral analyses, temperature/entropy investigations, and degeneration examples are retained. The new External Collapse Indicators paragraph discusses existing Figures 2–3 and Appendix C rather than introducing another analysis.

E5.justification: The appendix still reports 96 completions and 25th–75th percentile bands. Table 1 and its accompanying discussion retain the same statistical reporting and Kolmogorov–Smirnov tests; no new run, seed, or uncertainty procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the plotted results are unchanged. Section 7 retains the reported 8% versus 56% non-collapse rates at temperature 0.7 and 5% versus 33% at entropy 1.0. Appendix results and qualitative examples also match.

T1.justification: Equation (9) receives a non-equivalent algebraic correction: the revised operator preserves components orthogonal to the regulated subspace, consistent with selective damping. The IFS mathematics, correlation-dimension definitions, generalized eigenproblem, and appendix derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central geometric-collapse hypothesis, inference-time RMR contribution, and claims of improved low-entropy generation without degraded surface quality are retained. The added qualifications do not redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly describes the IFS as a qualitative analogy, distinguishes the dimension threshold from complete text quality, and identifies untested application domains. It also discusses future training-analysis uses. Conversely, v1's caveat about architecture-dependent optimal regulation settings is replaced by emphasis on stability across tested settings.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-repository link on the first page. Figure 2's caption newly explains that panel (b) uses a separate trajectory at temperature 1.0, while panel (a) uses 0.5. Existing implementation details and appendix instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2.3 adds Takahashi and Tanaka-Ishii (2019) and Tanaka-Ishii (2026), connecting the work to scaling-law and repeated-subsequence diagnostics. This modestly broadens positioning while retaining the existing relationships to decoding controls and activation interventions.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized prose corrections and explanatory additions, adds acknowledgements, and replaces the preprint notice with conference publication information. The section organization and Appendices A–G remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 5 to page 6, and Table 1 moves from page 8 to page 9 with spacing changes. Figure 2's caption and Figure 4's panel wording are revised. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects Equation (9)'s inconsistency with selective damping, clarifies the toy model's status and Figure 2's settings, and supplies code-access information. These improve correctness and interpretability of the retained study. Removing the explicit caveat about architecture-dependent optimal settings slightly weakens caution, but the net improvement is supported and limited.
